newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SocGen analyst cautious on Roche buy.
newsitem.headline: SocGen analyst cautious on Roche buy.

text.p: Analyst Arnaud Delepine of Societe Generale Equities and Derivatives Research said he took a cautious view of Roche Holding AG's acquisition of Boehringer Mannheim and expected the deal to dilute earnings.
In a research note, Delepine said he doubted the acquisition would create the same scale of synergies as that of a pure pharmaceuticals group because:
Firstly, the fit between Roche and Boehringer is likely to be complementary rather than have areas of overlap, which would have opened the way for cost-cutting.
Secondly, the diagnostics market is difficult and highly competitive.
Other factors behind this view are that Roche will only gain two places in world ranking of pharmaceuticals groups to sixth from eighth.
The combined group will have a very strong presence in Germany, where cost-cutting takes longer than in the U.S.
Goodwill involved is likely to be considerable and this will cut into Roche's earnings growth.
To finance the acquisition Roche either will have to draw on its own cash reserves, which will reduce returns and thus dilute earnings, or make further calls on the market.
Boehringer's drugs portfolio includes recently-launched Reteplace, which is competition with Genentech's leading product.
